title: Sell Mineral Rights in Hickory, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Hickory, PA
metaDescription: Mineral owner near Hickory, Washington County? We buy oil, gas, and royalty interests near Hanover Township in the Marcellus wet-gas core. No pressure.
heroLead: Hickory sits in Hanover Township, right in the middle of one of Washington County's busiest Marcellus corridors.
intro: Hickory is an unincorporated community in Hanover Township, Washington County, an area that's been a steady focus of Marcellus horizontal drilling for years. Families with land here often hold interests in multiple pooled units, given how densely this part of the county has been developed.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Hickory, whether you're holding one producing interest or several across different units on family land.

sections.heading: Hanover Township's drilling density
paragraphs: This part of Washington County has seen enough horizontal development that it's common for a single family's acreage to touch more than one pooled unit, each with its own production history and lease terms.

sections.heading: Managing multiple interests from one tract
paragraphs: When a family holds pieces of several units, we review each one individually rather than treating the whole acreage as a single interest, since performance and terms can differ meaningfully between units.

sections.heading: What we need from you
paragraphs: Division orders and recent royalty statements for each unit help most, but we can work from whatever documentation you have and fill in gaps through county records.

We're comfortable coordinating review of multiple units at once so you get a clear picture across your whole family's holdings. Hickory-area families sometimes hold interests dating back to the very first Marcellus leasing wave in Hanover Township, and those original terms are worth comparing against anything signed more recently on the same land.

faqs.question: My Hickory-area land touches more than one drilling unit. How does that work?
faqs.answer: It's common in this densely developed part of Washington County. We review each unit separately, since production history and lease terms can differ between them even on adjacent acreage.

faqs.question: Do you need a division order for every unit my land is part of?
faqs.answer: It helps if you have them, but we can request the relevant division orders and lease documents through county records if you don't have copies for every unit.

faqs.question: Is Hickory in an actively producing part of the county?
faqs.answer: Yes, Hanover Township has been a consistent focus of Marcellus horizontal development in Washington County for years.

faqs.question: If I hold interests in two different Hickory-area units, can you buy both at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can review and make offers on multiple interests together, though we'll evaluate each unit's performance and terms individually since they can differ meaningfully even on adjoining acreage.
